What lawful usually means

You must be 18 or over, and a reputable shop will ask for an identity check. Sell only what you own, keep consent if another adult appears, and do not upload intimate images that were shared without consent.

Platform rules still bind you when the criminal law does not. Trafficking, exploitation and using the service to solicit prostitution are banned on the shops that bother to write terms.

The £1,000 allowance

The trading allowance can cover up to £1,000 of gross trading income a year, which is the total you receive before fees and costs. If every side hustle together stays at or under that line, you generally may not have to tell HMRC, and you still keep records.

You can still need to register under £1,000, for example if you already file Self Assessment, you want loss relief, or you want National Insurance treatment that depends on registering. One allowance covers all trading income, so £800 from content plus £500 from crafts is £1,300 and you tell HMRC.

Over £1,000 of gross trading income you generally register for Self Assessment. You can then deduct up to £1,000 instead of actual expenses, and you cannot claim both, so the choice is whichever your records support.

The UK tax year runs from 6 April to 5 April. If you need to register for a year that has just ended, tell HMRC by 5 October, then file and pay by 31 January.

A late return that you already had to file starts with a £100 penalty, with further charges if it stays late. Failing to tell HMRC you needed to register is a separate charge based on tax still unpaid, and it is not an automatic £100.

For 2026/27 the standard personal allowance is £12,570. In England, Wales and Northern Ireland the basic rate is 20 percent on taxable income from £12,571 to £50,270, and Scotland uses different bands.

That allowance applies to your job plus the side income. It is not a second exemption stacked on the trading allowance.

For 2026/27, Class 2 National Insurance is treated as paid if profits are £7,105 or more, which protects the record, and Class 4 is 6 percent between £12,570 and £50,270, then 2 percent above that. Making Tax Digital for Income Tax starts to bite at much higher qualifying income, so most casual sellers will not meet it.

FAQ

Is it legal to sell feet pics in the UK?

Adults 18 and over can generally sell lawful photos of their own feet, and the buyer's fetish is not what the obscenity test looks at. Criminal conduct, non-consent or anyone under 18 is a different matter, and this is not legal advice.

Do I pay tax if I sell feet pics?

HMRC can treat the money as trading income. The trading allowance covers up to £1,000 of gross trading income a year from all side hustles together, and you keep records either way.

When do I register for Self Assessment?

Generally when gross trading income goes over £1,000, with a notice by 5 October after the tax year and a file-and-pay date of 31 January. Some people still need to register under the allowance.

Are FeetFinder plans free in the UK?

Buyer accounts are free, and seller plans are not. Basic starts at $4.99 a month, with a 15 percent fee, or 10 percent on Premium.

Will a payout arrive in pounds?

FeetFinder transacts earnings in US dollars. A UK bank or e-wallet may add a conversion fee, and the usual payout request starts at $30.

Does a VPN make the income invisible to HMRC?

No, a VPN does not rewrite a payout or a platform report. The income is still taxable if the trading rules say it is.
